title: There’s a Planet Where It Rains Glass Sideways
start_frame_prompt: Ultra-photorealistic vertical cinematic view above the atmosphere of hot Jupiter exoplanet HD 189733 b, deep cobalt-blue planetary limb, turbulent silicate-rich cloud decks, harsh stellar illumination from nearby orange-white star, physically motivated atmospheric haze and scattering, premium space documentary realism, no text, no fantasy rings, no Earth continents.
negative_prompt: cartoon, infographic, labels, literal household window glass shards, fantasy crystal storm, neon, game render, Earth surface, astronaut, text, watermark, malformed planet, black bars
narration: This blue world looks beautiful, but its weather is brutal. HD 189733 b is a scorching gas giant about sixty-four light-years away. Its blue color is linked to silicate particles in the atmosphere. Models and observations suggest extreme winds racing around the planet at thousands of kilometers per hour. In that heat, silicate material can condense into glass-like particles. Driven by those winds, the storm would sweep them almost sideways. The famous phrase 'raining glass' is shorthand — not ordinary window shards falling from a sky.
captions: THIS BLUE PLANET IS NOT PEACEFUL.
HD 189733 b: A SCORCHING GAS GIANT.
SILICATE PARTICLES HELP MAKE IT BLUE.
EXTREME WINDS DRIVE THE STORM SIDEWAYS.

scenes.prompt: Start from the exact orbital reference and dive toward HD 189733 b's cobalt atmospheric limb. Camera passes continuously into turbulent high clouds with realistic scale, scattering and enormous wind-sheared cloud bands. No solid ground appears because this is a gas giant. Preserve star direction and blue atmospheric identity; premium NASA-documentary visual realism, no labels.

Continue inside the same atmosphere. Camera tracks laterally through violently sheared blue-gray clouds while tiny hot silicate condensate particles stream nearly horizontally with the wind. Particles are microscopic-to-grain-scale glass-like material, not giant sharp household shards. Show physically coherent turbulence, depth and motion blur; no fantasy crystal cave, no cut.

Impossible macro camera follows a cluster of silicate vapor cooling and condensing into translucent glass-like droplets and grains within the hot atmosphere. Maintain connection to the surrounding storm through visible cloud depth. Realistic refraction and high-temperature haze, no arrows, chemical labels, diagrams or magical sparkle. The particles immediately accelerate with the lateral flow.

Pull back from macro scale to an immense atmospheric storm corridor. Countless tiny silicate particles race almost sideways across frame within supersonic-scale winds, with layered cloud bands stretching around the curved planet. Camera banks smoothly with the flow. Keep particles small and physically plausible; no person, spacecraft impact, ground, giant glass blades or sensational gore.

Camera exits the storm continuously back above the blue limb, revealing huge wind bands wrapping around HD 189733 b while the star illuminates the atmosphere. End on a premium photoreal planetary hero shot that contrasts beautiful cobalt color with violent weather. No generated text, no rings, no Earth-like oceans, no fantasy lightning unless physically subtle.

production_notes.director_intent: Beauty-to-danger reveal. The hook is the impossible dive from blue orbital beauty into a sideways silicate storm.
production_notes.science_guard: Avoid presenting literal window-glass shards as directly observed rain. Phrase as glass-like silicate condensate/particles inferred from atmospheric conditions; winds are extreme and planet is a hot Jupiter.
production_notes.sound_design: Natural documentary narration plus restrained low atmospheric roar as cinematic representation; no screams or glass-breaking Foley.
